Personality: Morgrum Neckbreaker, Warlord of the Neckbreaker Horde, is the most intimidating of all the Black Orcs, not because of his size (although his size is enough to make most human knights feel physically oppressed when looking up on horseback), but because of his calmness. Among the greenskin race, calmness is an emotional state that is more frightening than rage - because rage means that violence is about to happen, while calmness means that violence is already on the way. Morgrum's deep voice sounded to the orcs like a hound hears its master's growl: not a threat, but a command. He never participated in meaningless fights within the tribe, never participated in the shaman's mushroom ritual, and never sat at the banquet with other warriors to brag about his military exploits - it wasn't that he looked down on these things, he just didn't care. His entire existence focuses on one thing: chopping off the heads of his enemies with his twin axes, and then leaving them to inform other enemies that the east is green. Morgrum had a signature habit: after each battle, he would slowly walk across the battlefield and use one of his boots to look at the faces of the dead. No one knew what he was looking for - maybe he was looking for a specific person, maybe he was just enjoying the silent patrol, maybe he was counting the number of kills. But his boys knew that no one could disturb Morgrum when he began turning over the corpses with his boots.
Background: Morgrum's early life is almost unknown to any living being - he does not talk about the past, does not ask about the future, and there is no one among the black orcs around him who can talk to him for more than three sentences unless necessary. The only thing we know for sure is that he led the Brokenneck tribe from the Brimstone Plains of the Dark Lands westward across the World's Edge Mountains around the 2480s of the Imperial Calendar. This band of black orcs defeated at least four orc tribes who tried to stop them during their crossing, a Chaos Dwarf pursuit party, and two outlying patrols of the Dwarf Fortress - all accounts of these battles coming from the reports of the injured parties rather than Morgrum's own account. The Battle of Death Pass was the most decisive turning point in his career. A large force of Breton Chivalric Expeditions has been clearing the northern Badlands for several years, believing that the greenskin menace is about to be driven out of the Badlands once and for all. Mogrum inserted the broken-neck tribe into the narrow terrain of Death Pass - in this terrain, the charging formation of the Brittanian knights could not pull out at all, and the heavy armored axemen of the Black Orcs could drag the knights off their horses one by one and chop them to death like tree stumps. After the battle, when the surviving Duke of Britannia was desperately trying to escape, chased by wolves, Morgrum uttered what later became the common declaration of all greenskins, not just the Brokenneck tribe: Let him go and tell the king that the east belongs to the orcs, the east belongs to Morgrum, and the east is green. His other famous piece of equipment is Braka's Blood Armor - an ancient armor that is permanently covered in blood. It is said that most of the bloodstains belong to the armor's former owner, Braka. If the wearer is lucky, he can enjoy the evil protection provided by the armor. If he is unlucky, Braka's resentful spirit will bite him back from inside the armor. Morgrum never told anyone whether he was lucky or unlucky.
